title: Losing months: 2 of 12 months ended in a net loss
details: 2026-04: net loss $14,120.00 on revenue of $71,100.00 (northstar_profit_and_loss_oct2025-sep2026.xlsx, Sheet "Profit and Loss" row 27, column H (Apr 2026)) | 2026-07: net loss $14,740.00 on revenue of $75,700.00 (northstar_profit_and_loss_oct2025-sep2026.xlsx, Sheet "Profit and Loss" row 27, column K (Jul 2026))
fix: Open the loss months side by side with your best months and list every cost line that did not shrink with revenue. | Set a break-even revenue target per month (fixed costs divided by your gross margin) and track bookings against it weekly. | Fill slow months: schedule maintenance-agreement visits, tune-ups and promotions before the slow season starts.
prevention: Review the P&L within 10 days of each month-end; act mid-month when bookings run below break-even. | Re-bid fixed costs (insurance, software, vehicles) annually with slow-season revenue in mind.

Hoffman: $1,280.00 outstanding, due 2026-09-10 (36 days overdue)
fix: Call every invoice over 30 days overdue this week, starting with the largest; agree a payment date in writing. | Send statements with a pay-now link (card or ACH) and offer a short payment plan for the largest balance. | Pause new non-emergency work for accounts more than 60 days overdue until they are current.
prevention: Turn on automatic reminders at 3 days before, on, and 7/14/30 days after the due date. | Collect deposits on installs and require card-on-file for residential service. | Review A/R aging every Monday.

title: Overtime: 14.1% of gross wages paid as overtime
formula: overtime pay / 3 (the half-time premium at time-and-a-half)
details: Overtime pay $16,842.75 of $119,322.75 gross wages; the premium portion above straight time is about $5,614.25. | Jake Lindgren: 147 overtime hours vs 560 regular hours (26.3%), $8,379.00 overtime pay | Marcus Olson: 141 overtime hours vs 560 regular hours (25.2%), $7,719.75 overtime pay
fix: Shift routine maintenance calls to slower days and stop booking non-emergency work after 3 pm for the overloaded techs. | Compare the overtime premium with the cost of hiring or subcontracting one more tech. | Require approval for overtime beyond 5 hours per week per person.
prevention: Review overtime by employee every payroll and set a weekly cap. | Track billable hours per tech to spot overload early.

fix: Plan routes so techs go job to job, and stock vans so they do not return to the shop for parts. | Review non-billable hours with each tech weekly.

title: Card processing fees: 3.5% effective rate vs 2.9% target
formula: total fees - gross volume x target rate
details: Total fees $20,451.32 on $576,096.00 gross volume across 12 payout rows. | At a 2.9% rate the same volume would cost $16,706.78.
fix: Request an interchange-plus quote from your current processor and two competitors using the last 12 months of volume. | Push large commercial invoices to ACH/bank transfer instead of card. | Add a compliant card surcharge or cash-discount program if allowed in your state.
prevention: Check the effective rate (fees / gross) on every monthly statement. | Review processor pricing once a year.

title: Fuel up 53.8% while revenue changed -19.6%
formula: sum(last 3 months) - sum(first 3 months) for this cost line
fix: Pull every Fuel transaction for the last 3 months and tag each as necessary, reducible or cancel. | Route calls by area each morning and stock vans to avoid trips back to the shop; use a fuel card with per-vehicle reports. | Set a monthly budget for Fuel tied to revenue and review it at month-end.
prevention: Track Fuel as a percent of revenue each month and investigate any month above the prior quarter's average. | Require owner approval for new recurring charges.

title: Possible duplicate charges: 2 repeated charge(s)
formula: sum of the second charge in each same-vendor, same-amount pair within 3 days
details: HOME DEPOT #2231: $612.48 charged twice around 2026-07-14 (northstar_credit_card_apr-sep2026.csv, CSV row 32) | FERGUSON SUPPLY #4471 ACH: $2,418.37 charged twice around 2026-09-09 (northstar_bank_statement_sep2026.pdf, page 1, line 12)
fix: Match each pair to the vendor invoice; if only one invoice exists, request a refund or credit in writing. | For card charges, dispute the duplicate with the card issuer if the vendor does not refund within 10 days.
prevention: Pay vendors from one method only and record the invoice number in the payment memo. | Review bank and card activity weekly for repeated amounts.

title: Marketing return: Facebook Ads, Angi Leads cost more than the jobs they brought in
formula: per source: spend - max(0, sum(job revenue - labor - materials) of jobs with that lead source in the same months)
details: Facebook Ads: spent $1,260.00 in 2026-07, 2026-08, 2026-09; 5 job(s) contributed $662.00; shortfall $598.00. | Angi Leads: spent $2,340.00 in 2026-07, 2026-08, 2026-09; 2 job(s) contributed $749.00; shortfall $1,591.00. | Google Ads: spend $1,950.00, 8 attributed job(s), job contribution $2,604.00 | Facebook Ads: spend $1,260.00, 5 attributed job(s), job contribution $662.00 | Angi Leads: spend $2,340.00, 2 attributed job(s), job contribution $749.00
fix: Pause or cut the budget on the losing sources for one month and watch booked jobs. | Move the budget to the source with the best contribution per dollar.
prevention: Record the lead source on every job and review spend vs contribution by source monthly.

details: J-3110 (Water heater install): billed $1,720.00, margin $140.00 (8.1%) | J-3115 (Water heater install): billed $1,790.00, margin $160.00 (8.9%) | J-3124 (Water heater install): billed $1,760.00, margin $155.00 (8.8%)

title: Overlapping subscriptions: QUICKFLEET GPS MONTHLY and FLEETTRACK PRO GPS

title: Rising recurring charges: 1 vendor(s) raised their price
formula: sum over later months of (monthly charge - first monthly charge)
fix: Log in to each vendor and check plan, seats and add-ons; remove unused users. | Ask for the original price or an annual-prepay discount; get quotes from one alternative to negotiate.
prevention: Keep a subscription list with owner, price and renewal date; review it quarterly. | Use one company card for subscriptions with alerts for any amount change.
